title: Conditional required-field rules are forked between Properties.tsx (1811-line god-module) and blockSummary.ts — and the copies have already diverged
existing_state: The per-block conditional required logic (readfile path/into/path_into, http auth modes, interactive show_window bounds) exists twice: `isPropertyRequired` inside panels/Properties.tsx:870-923 and `isRequired` in utils/blockSummary.ts:22-43 — the latter's own comment admits it was 'ported from Properties.isPropertyRequired'. They have already drifted: Properties gained an `isDynamicRuntimeValue(auth)` guard for `${var}` auth values (Properties.tsx:866-868,894) that blockSummary never received. Today the outcome difference is latent only because http's username/password/token are not statically required (blockDefs/registry.ts:366-369), so the next rule added or flag flipped in one copy makes the on-canvas expanded summary card (which renders '— not set' badges from blockSummary, BaseBlock.tsx:180-182) disagree with the Properties panel's validation about the same block. The duplication exists because the rules live inside a 1811-line component file (Properties.tsx also contains useBufferedInput, ChoiceOptionsEditor, the group resolver, browse-path correlation, StartProperties, and the Test Block UI), which a plain util can't import without dragging the whole panel in.
recommendation: Extract `isPropertyRequired` + its `toBoolean`/`hasAnyValue`/`isDynamicRuntimeValue` helpers into a leaf module (e.g. utils/propertyRules.ts) and have both Properties.tsx and blockSummary.ts consume it — that alone removes the fork. While there, split Properties.tsx along its existing seams (useBufferedInput → hooks/, ChoiceOptionsEditor and StartProperties → own files); each is already self-contained, so it's mechanical.
user_benefit: Required/validation rules are the contract between what the canvas card warns about and what the panel enforces; one authoritative module means a rule added for a new block can't silently apply in only one of the two surfaces.
